summary.methodology: Prices were gathered from BLS Feb 2026 national averages, direct store website data, and multiple price comparison articles (NPR, Cheapism, WCPO, Chowhound, Easy Family Budgeting). For items without direct pricing data, estimates were calculated using Consumer Reports' Feb 2026 price index ratios vs Walmart: Kroger +15%, Target +6%, Whole Foods +28%, Aldi -7%, Lidl -6%. Estimated items are marked with estimated: true. Prices re-verified 2026-03-28 using Ramsey Solutions (May 2025), WCPO Cincinnati (Oct 2025), KCL (Dec 2025), Easy Family Budgeting (Dec 2025), Cheapism (Oct 2025), and web searches.
notes: BLS national average prices (Feb 2026) served as the baseline for US retail food prices
Walmart consistently had the lowest or near-lowest prices on most staples
Aldi prices are competitive with or below Walmart on store-brand items
Whole Foods prices are typically 25-35% higher than Walmart, reflecting organic/premium positioning
Lidl has very limited online pricing data - most Lidl prices are estimated based on Aldi pricing +1-3%
Kroger is approximately 15% more expensive than Walmart on average per Consumer Reports 2026
Target is approximately 6% more expensive than Walmart on average
Meat prices (especially beef) saw significant increases in 2025-2026 due to reduced cattle herds
Egg prices dropped dramatically from 2025 highs ($5.90/doz) to $2.50 in Feb 2026
Coffee prices rose ~30% YoY due to climate disruptions in Brazil
